=== DOCS-TRUTH ANCHORS (re-verified, no edits required) ===

• concat_ws-skips-NULL (docs-truth): `concat_ws(separator, string1, ..., stringN) -> varchar` skips NULL string args (not the separator — NULL separator → NULL result). Verbatim from trino.io/docs/current/functions/string.html. Distinct from plain `concat()` / `||` which propagate NULL (any NULL operand → NULL result). Resource landing: r27:985 + r27:999 + r27:1421 + r27:1552. The fix for "full display name from first_name + last_name skipping NULLs" is `concat_ws(' ', first_name, last_name)` — single function, NULL-skip built-in, no COALESCE wrap needed (unlike `||` which would need `COALESCE(first_name,'') || ' ' || COALESCE(last_name,'')` AND would still leave a stray separator on NULL-skip cases — `concat_ws` handles that cleanly).

• approx_percentile-ARRAY-form (docs-truth): `approx_percentile(x, percentages) -> array<[same as x]>` — multiple percentiles in ONE pass via `ARRAY[0.5, 0.9]` arg, returns array aligned to input. One sketch, one shuffle, N numbers out. Verbatim from trino.io/docs/current/functions/aggregate.html (overload #2 of 4). Resource landing: r23:161-165 (signature pin) + r23:145/154 (worked examples) + r05:2253 (multi-tenant example). The fix for "median AND 90th percentile latency in one row" is `approx_percentile(latency, ARRAY[0.5, 0.9]) AS p50_p90 FROM ...` — single aggregate, single scan, returns `ARRAY[median, p90]`. To get them as separate columns, project `[1]` and `[2]` from the array: `p[1] AS p50, p[2] AS p90`.

• orders-above-category-avg (docs-truth): The clean form computes AVG per category in a CTE/subquery via `AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS cat_avg`, then filters at the OUTER level: `WITH p AS (SELECT *, AVG(price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS cat_avg FROM products) SELECT * FROM p WHERE price > cat_avg;`. NOT a window function in WHERE — that is rejected by Trino 467 analyzer (verified at trino.io/docs/467/sql/select.html — WHERE runs BEFORE window evaluation in clause-evaluation order). Resource landing: r23:937-1010 LEADING CANONICAL (iter637 PIN — wrap-the-window-then-compare) covers `MAX / MIN / AVG over PARTITION BY` explicitly at r23:941. Alternative form via GROUP BY + JOIN: `SELECT p.* FROM products p JOIN (SELECT category, AVG(price) AS cat_avg FROM products GROUP BY category) c ON p.category = c.category WHERE p.price > c.cat_avg;` — equivalent semantics; window form is cheaper (one scan vs join).
